### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict (symbol, a top-level type))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `47a2be3ccc9e0aa683251d0f764f440476778b0e` — the merge of head `fa9ec1d75754ff456e83347ee018c27023b054cd` into base `9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 47a2be3ccc9e0aa683251d0f764f440476778b0e && git checkout 47a2be3ccc9e0aa683251d0f764f440476778b0e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99 fa9ec1d75754ff456e83347ee018c27023b054cd && git checkout -B drift-repro 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99 && git merge --no-ff fa9ec1d75754ff456e83347ee018c27023b054cd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa9ec1d75754ff456e83347ee018c27023b054cd`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #23001's body and its four comments (claim 6121333983 as corrected, os-dev-report 6122615428, seat answer 6122658288, patch round 1 6122690936); PR #23023's body, its one comment (docs-drift bot 6122548820), its five-file list and the net diff of `refs/review/pr-23023` against `origin/main` (merge base `4e6b270999`; 5 files, +448/−26); the check-runs on the head; on `origin/main`: `artifact-forward-conversion.ts`, the door in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/` (registry, types, apply), `protocol-handshake.ts`, ADR-0087; the cited precedent #20390 / PR #20435 (`e956924e17`, its changeset read off the commit).

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Accept set at the artifact door (widening, intended).** `applyArtifactForwardConversions` now answers `'converted-major-step'` for a floor of `M.0.0` at or above the runtime label and replays every `retiredFromLoadPath` entry with `toMajor === M`, default flips refused by id first. On this tree that is every `^18` artifact on a runtime labelled 17.7.0 through 18.0.0, which previously got `'authored-current'` and no replay. Judged right: it is the card's done-criterion, ADR-0087's at-rest supersession text covers it, and the per-entry comparison cannot reach it — measured on `origin/main`'s registry: 66 retired step-18 entries, 0 live step-18 entries, every `retiredAfter` between 17.0.0 and 17.7.0, none at or above 18. Code shape: `idsTheFloorPostdates` reads `firstReleaseOfMajor = floor[1] === 0 && floor[2] === 0` and classifies each non-flip retired entry as per-entry `opened` (floor at or below `retiredAfter`), else `majorStep` (first release and `toMajor === floor[0]`), else `closed`; live entries stay closed as before. The branch is reached only when the floor is not below the runtime label, so that half of the condition is positional, not re-tested — correct. A `^99.0.0` floor still answers `'authored-current'` (no step-99 entries) and its existing pin stands. Per-entry is read before major-step, so an entry open under both would be listed once with its `retiredAfter`; on this tree no entry is open under both.

2. **Reading (ii), idempotence, is proven over the real entries in both directions.** The whole-step block in `artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts` iterates `ALL_CONVERSIONS` filtered by `toMajor === 18 && retiredFromLoadPath === true`: each entry's `fixture.before` under a `^18` manifest converts to exactly its `fixture.after` with `expectedNotices` all from that entry (the single step-18 default flip, `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`, comes back by reference), and each `fixture.after` with the whole step replayed comes back by the same reference with zero notices. Because it iterates the registry, #22990's entry and any later step-18 retirement are covered the day they land with no edit here. Judged right. Caveat, which the PR body states and which does not contradict the card: the pins prove "an artifact WITHOUT the retired shape is unchanged". For the component-prop family in step 18 (`object-grid-default-filters-removed`, `object-grid-default-sort-removed`, `object-kanban-quick-add-removed`, `page-header-breadcrumb-removed`, the `element-*` and `record:*` entries and their siblings) the door's strict parse does not refuse the old key, because `PageComponent.properties` is a `z.record` carrier — so a `^18` artifact built AFTER such a retirement can still carry the inert key, and the replay now rewrites it to the canonical spelling (for `defaultFilters`: moved into an empty `filter`, deleted beside a populated one). That is a change to a post-retirement artifact, but only of a key no renderer reads, in the rescue direction; the chain already does the same to that key for every `^17.x` floor and every stored row, and `DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE` is unchanged, so no reinterpretation class enters. The card's "replaying an entry over an artifact without the retired key changes nothing" holds.

3. **The new verdict and `replayedRetirements`.** `'converted-major-step'` is chosen whenever `majorStep` is non-empty, else `'converted-retired-after'`. `replayedRetirements` lists only the per-entry half's entries (empty under the new verdict on this tree, pinned `toEqual(openedByRule('18.0.0'))`), so its invariant — each row carries a `retiredAfter` the floor is at or below — holds. In `_convertArtifactForward` a major-step replay therefore takes the second log form, which prescribes rebuilding with current tooling — right for a prerelease build. Judged right.

4. **GA behaviour.** At label 18.0.0 the floor equals the label, the `else` branch is reached, step 18 replays and the verdict is `'converted-major-step'`; from 18.0.1 the floor is below the label and the verdict is `'converted-forward'`. Pinned at labels 17.7.0, 18.0.0-next.0 and 18.0.0, and at 18.0.1 (`parseVersion` tolerates the prerelease tail). Judged right. Noted, not a defect: from this PR on every `^18` artifact runs the 65-entry replay at boot where `'authored-current'` previously skipped `applyConversions`; the dev's corroboration over the three example stacks found 0 notices and the same reference.

5. **The protocol-18 handshake is untouched.** `protocol-handshake.ts` is not in the file list; `checkProtocolCompat` still reads `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (18.0.0 on `origin/main`) through `rangeAdmitsMajor`, so `^17` is refused with `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` and `objectstack migrate meta --from 17` before the door runs, and `^18` is admitted. The CONTROL pin passes `'18.0.0'` explicitly, so it pins the function rather than the constant — acceptable, since the diff touches nothing in `packages/spec`.

6. **#20390's 17.x-floor path is unchanged.** For a floor that is not `M.0.0` the new `else if` never fires, so `^17.7.0` on a 17.7.0 label answers as before (`'converted-retired-after'` when `openedByRule` is non-empty, else `'authored-current'`), and `permission-allow-restore-purge-removed` (stamped 17.2.0) is not replayed for it; pinned as CONTROL, and the existing per-entry block is untouched in the diff. Judged right.

7. **The rewritten existing pin.** `REFUSES the amnesty for an artifact authored at a NEWER spec than the runtime` modelled "newer" as `^18.0.0` on a 17.2.0 label; on this tree that input is the card's defect, so the pin pinned the defect. It now uses `currentSurfaceFloor('17.2.0')` (the maximum of the label and every `retiredAfter`, patch plus one; 17.7.1 today), guards that it does not end in `.0.0`, and keeps the `'authored-current'` and same-reference assertions. Forced by the design, not a weakening. Judged right.

8. **The `packages/metadata` surface breach.** `FORWARD_WINDOW_OPENED` is a total `Record` over `ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict`, so the new member does not compile without a row; the open side keeps the table's stated invariant (the #12915 bare-root form-predicate notice reads the same window as the replay). Consequence: that warn-only notice now also fires for a `^18` artifact carrying bare-root predicates, as it already does for every `^17.0.0`-stamped app on a 17.7.0 runtime — no new class. `artifactWindowClause` gains a branch because both existing clauses print a false sentence for a floor above the label. The new test file pins the card's "named in the boot log" criterion on the real `MetadataPlugin._parseAndRegisterArtifact`. All three are in the `domain:engine` lane; the claim's "stop on a breach and explain it" was followed in the report and the seat accepted it. Judged right.

9. **Could a `^18` artifact that boots now carry anything the door used to refuse besides retired keys?** No. The replay set is exactly the retired step-18 entries minus the refused flips, and each rewrites only the old shape it positively recognises — retired keys and retired value shapes (a bare `unique: true`, a string sort clause, a UTC-suffixed time default, a string-list `manifest.permissions`). Everything else still meets `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` and `EnvironmentArtifactSchema` strictly. The runtime's second door (`AppPlugin`, the security bundle) consumes the same function and reads `verdict` only into a debug log; no exhaustive switch over the union exists in-tree outside `FORWARD_WINDOW_OPENED`.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: `minor`, `Clause-②: yes` — the true value. `ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict` is exported from the package root (`export * from './artifact-forward-conversion.js'`), a consumer can now receive a value it could not before, and a TS exhaustive switch gains an arm: a public-surface enlargement, so `yes`, and `yes` takes at least `minor`. The precedent is the same shape: PR #20435's changeset (`e956924e17`) reads `'@objectstack/metadata-core': minor`, `'@objectstack/metadata': patch`, `Clause-②: yes`, with the identical consumer sentence; its BREAKING banner and `adr-0087: not-required` marker belonged to the `MetadataConversion` type change in `packages/spec`, which this PR has no counterpart of.
- `@objectstack/metadata`: `patch` — the true value. No exported surface changes; the table row and clause are internal, and the behaviour change is a boot-log clause plus a warn that now also reaches `^18` artifacts.
- The PR body's second line, the changeset body and the corrected claim all read `Clause-②: yes`; `Check Changeset` is green on this head. Under `.changeset/pre.json` (`mode: pre`, tag `next`) the published label does not move with the level, which changes what ships, not what the declaration must say.
- ADR-0087 markers. The changeset disposition marker is NOT owed: no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner, and the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` run reports no declared-breaking changeset. An ADR-0087 amendment note IS owed as a follow-up: the 2026-09-13 addendum's window bullet (as amended 2026-09-30) states the rule as two disjuncts and its closing paragraph says the window "is for within-line retirements"; both sentences are now narrower than the code. The ADR names the module docblock as the rule's authority, the docblock carries the third disjunct and the M2 caveat, and `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, so the note cannot ride this PR without making it Tier H — the precedent carried #20390's note in a separate governed docs PR (`4cc5bcd858`, #20797) two days after the code landed. Escalated in ③; not a blocker.

### ③ Boundary flags

Round-0 report (6122615428):
- `deviations[0]` FILE-SURFACE BREACH (`plugin.ts` row and clause, new metadata test) — answered: compile-forced and lane-internal; right (① item 8).
- `deviations[1]` changeset names `@objectstack/metadata` at `patch` — answered: consequence of the breach, identical to the precedent; right.
- `deviations[2]` pin subject swapped from #22990's email-template keys (unlanded) to `declared-index-unique-scope` — answered: right; the whole-step block covers #22990's entry automatically when it lands.
- `deviations[3]` existing pin rewritten — answered: right (① item 7).
- `deviations[4]` zero label writes — answered: nothing owed; `skip-changeset` does not apply to a publishing diff.
- `deviations[5]` `origin/main` merged before the PR opened, no os-regen deferral — answered: the §10 shape; the merge commit `335aaf9ad7` is on the branch and the net diff against the merge base is the five intended files.
- `deviations[6]` attribution — answered: all five non-merge commits carry the model-free trailer pair (verified on the fetched ref) and the PR body ends with the session-URL footer; AGENTS.md wins over the harness reminder; right.
- `open_questions[0]` Clause-② and the bump — settled by the seat as option B (6122658288); this review confirms B against the precedent (②).
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (class a, filed as #23025): spec's `retired-after.census.test.ts` `triple()` throws on a prerelease label, so the census is red on any `18.0.0-next.N` tree and a retirement landing then cannot carry a stable stamp. Does not touch this diff: the major-step half matches on `toMajor`, not `retiredAfter`, and the door's `parseVersion` tolerates the prerelease tail (pinned at `18.0.0-next.0`). It does touch the per-entry half's input discipline on the next Version Packages PR — that card's concern, not this one's.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (class b, filed as #23026): a retired component prop (`object-grid` `defaultFilters`) passes `defineStack` and the door's strict parse through the `z.record` carrier, with only a lint warning. Does not touch this diff's lines; it bears on ① item 2's caveat (a post-retirement `^18` artifact can still carry such a key and the replay now canonicalises it), judged the rescue direction. The PR body records it under Acceptance notes as "noted, not filed"; the seat filed it, which is the better disposition.

Round-1 report (6122690936):
- `deviations[0]` the PR body's second line read `no` beside a `minor` changeset until the seat's edit — resolved: the body reads `Clause-②: yes` at the final read and `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

Escalations for the seat (none blocks the verdict):
- File the ADR-0087 follow-up: an amendment note under the 2026-09-13 addendum's window bullet naming the third disjunct (floor equals `M.0.0` and the entry's `toMajor` is `M`), the verdict `'converted-major-step'`, the M2 caveat, and the correction to "within-line retirements", as a docs-only Tier H PR the way #20797 carried #20390's note.
- Docs-drift comment 6122548820: one release-owned page names `ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict`; read-only and advisory, nothing to do on this PR.

Check-runs on the head at the final read — green: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, the claim, card and single-writer-path guards, `filter`; skipped: `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`; still pending: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (1/6)` through `Test Core (6/6)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)` and `(3/3)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Type Check · workspace`. Nothing red. The Tier S landing needs every check green beside this record, so the pending set is the seat's remaining wait; no monitor was started here. PR state at the final read: draft, auto-merge unarmed, head repo equals base repo, 474 changed lines, no governed path in the file list.
